title: recall, cloud-search and loss-decomp leave out families missing a cutoff for any tool
body:
## What exists today

recall, cloud-search and loss-decomp each read `data/mgy-cutoffs.tbl` through their own `Cutoffs::read(path, c, queries)` in `src/scores/mod.rs`. Each looks up a hit's cutoff with `Cutoffs::get(tool, query) -> Option<f32>`. `parse` turns a 0.0 cell into `None` with `.filter(|s| *s > 0.0)`. A family with no row also gets `None`. A hit whose cutoff is `None` fails `is_some_and(|c| best >= c)`, and nothing warns.

The result is that a family with no hmmer cutoff adds nothing to the truth. In a family with no nail cutoff, every hmmer hit counts as one nail missed. cloud-search has no hmmer column, so its `Tool::Hmmer` takes nail's cutoff.

The table promoted in `4424213` has 14 such families. All 14 have a 0.0 `nail_3`, and 9 of them also have a 0.0 `mmseqs_3`. Every one of them has a hmmer cutoff.

## Proposal

Jack decided this. A family that lacks a cutoff for any tool is left out of every count, for every tool. Whenever a pipeline leaves a family out, it reports how many hits it left out, per tool.

The outputs it changes:

- recall: the `pass` string written in `shard.rs`, and `summary.tbl`
- cloud-search: `summary.tbl` and `stages.tbl`
- loss-decomp: `stages.tbl`, `cutoff-pairs.tbl` and `depth.tbl`

Each benchmark keeps its own copy of the change, under the rule in `CLAUDE.md` that benchmarks share no analysis code.

## Open

- Where the count goes: a `#=` line in each table, or a line from `parse` on stderr.
- Whether "any tool" means every tool the table holds, or only the tools a run reads. cloud-search reads no hmmer column.
- Whether a left-out hit is any pair the tool reported in that family, or only pairs over some score.

notes.author: jackroddy/6422e305
notes.text:
Jack decided where the counts go.

- A table with a row per run gets a `left_out` column, holding the hits that run reported in the left-out families. These are recall's and cloud-search's `summary.tbl`, and loss-decomp's `stages.tbl` and `depth.tbl`. Each is under 20 KB today.
- A table with a row per pair gets one `#= left_out` line with a count per tool and no new column. These are recall's `scores.tbl` at 311 GB, and loss-decomp's `runs.tbl`, `hits.tbl`, `lists.tbl` and `cutoff-pairs.tbl`.
- Every one of these tables also gets `#= left_out families <n>`.
